document.title: IIR [Excised] Pakistani Political, Military Situation, and Terrorism Issues
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Secret] Discusses the political and military situation in Pakistan, including government stability, armed forces capabilities and terrorism issues in the post-September 11 climate.

organizations.name: Defense Intelligence Agency
organizations.notes: Originator of the information report (FM DIA IMADS WASHINGTON DC).

organizations.name: Pakistani Armed Forces
organizations.notes: Report states they are the only formation capable of overthrowing the Pakistani government.

organizations.name: Government of Pakistan
organizations.notes: Described as stable; would not officially hide Taliban/al-Qaeda terrorists unless beneficial to its security interests.

organizations.name: Pakistani intelligence organization
organizations.notes: Report says no chance that groups in Pakistan, including the intelligence organization, would overthrow the government. The ISI is not named in the text.

organizations.name: Taliban
organizations.notes: Report discusses fear in Pakistan about the consequences of Taliban/al-Qaeda defeat.

organizations.name: al-Qa'ida
organizations.notes: Referred to as Taliban/al-Qaeda forces and terrorists.

organizations.name: Pakistani organizations providing shelter and support
organizations.notes: Unnamed; the report says many organizations within Pakistan would shelter and support Taliban/al-Qaeda terrorists.

events.description: Date of report information (DOR 20020106). The report was originated 7 Jan 2002 and disseminated 9 Jan 2002.
DIA information report on Pakistani political and military situation and terrorism issues; assessed government stable and Taliban/al-Qa'ida shelter by Pakistani organizations.

sources_cited: DIA Information Report (IIR) 02 8351472, DOR 6 Jan 2002; source excised
key_claims: The Pakistani government was stable and no internal group, including the intelligence organization, could overthrow it.
Only the Pakistani armed forces were capable of overthrowing the government.
Many in Pakistan feared that defeating Taliban/al-Qaeda forces would trigger more attacks on Westerners in Pakistan.
The Pakistani government would not officially hide Taliban/al-Qaeda terrorists unless it served its security interests.
Many organizations within Pakistan would shelter and support Taliban/al-Qaeda terrorists.
Lower-class Pakistanis viewed those the West calls terrorists as freedom fighters or fellow Muslim fighters.
